posts.title: Retired Black Athletes Turn Playing Careers Into Boardroom Empires
posts.description: A powerful cohort of retired African American athletes has redefined the narrative of the financially troubled former pro, turning short-term playing salaries into long-term corporate equity , venture funds, and extensive franchise portfolios. One of them is Hall of Fame basketball center Shaquille O’Neal. During a November 2026 appearance on Travis Chappell’s Dinner Party podcast , O’Neal revealed that a conservative financial backup plan he established years ago is projected to pay him roughly $1 million a month starting when he turns 55. posts.title: Gooru AI Launches Platform To Turn Human Expertise Into Digital Assistants
posts.description: Dallas-based artificial intelligence startup Gooru AI has launched a platform to help entrepreneurs, businesses, and organizations expand access to their expertise without increasing staffing levels, Dallas Innovates reports. Co-founded by former Microsoft executive Raamel Mitchell and technology entrepreneur Ankit Mehra, Gooru AI introduced its platform on Oct. 26 . The company, a participant in the Microsoft for Startups program, seeks to help organizations meet demand for customer support, education, and professional guidance. How Does Gooru AI Work? The platform allows users to create AI-powered representatives , known as Digital Goorus, using existing materials such as websites, training documents, and organizational policies. posts.title: Congress To Welcome Largest Class Of New Black Democrats In More Than 30 Years
posts.description: Congress will welcome 13 newly elected Black Democrats in January, marking the largest incoming class of Black Democratic lawmakers since 1993, following the November midterm elections, Reuters reports. The Congressional Black Caucus is expected to reach a record 64 members, up from 62, according to the outlet. Economic inequality, healthcare costs, and voting rights are among the policy issues facing the incoming lawmakers. Congressional Black Caucus Chair Rep. Yvette Clarke, D-N.Y., identified affordability as a top concern among constituents. The election results also set a record for Black representation in the Senate. Seven Black senators will serve concurrently following the election of Illinois Democrat Juliana Stratton and Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom. Colom will become Mississippi’s first Black senator in more than 140 years. The incoming class includes several younger lawmakers.
